page_objective: Define how SIPANEL layouts, components, content, imagery, technical diagrams, and conversion elements adapt across mobile, tablet, and desktop environments.

responsive_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL responsive behavior must preserve engineering clarity, technical readability, and conversion access across every screen size.

mobile: Keep primary CTA visible above fold.
Use accordions for dense technical content.
desktop: Allow split layouts and multi-column sections.
Use wider technical visuals where readability improves.

header.mobile: Logo left, menu icon right, language selector inside drawer, sticky CTA at bottom.
header.tablet: Logo left, collapsed or compact navigation, CTA visible.
header.desktop: Logo left, navigation center, CTA and language selector right.

hero.mobile: Stacked layout with headline, subheadline, CTA, trust items, then visual.
hero.tablet: Stacked or split layout depending on available width.
hero.desktop: Split 55/45 layout with text left and visual right.

trust_bar.mobile: Horizontal scroll metrics or compact 2x2 grid.

case_studies.mobile: Horizontal swipe cards with one visible card and card peek.
case_studies.desktop: Case study grid or slider with 3 visible cards.

forms.mobile: Step-based form with 1-2 inputs per screen.

technical_content_rules: Collapse secondary technical details on mobile.
Show summary before deep technical explanation.
Use progressive disclosure for complex engineering content.
Avoid exposing multiple dense diagrams at once.

mobile_behavior: Use no more than 3 visible callouts in preview mode.
tablet_behavior: Use preview modal or inline preview.
Allow zoom for dense technical diagrams.
desktop_behavior: Allow inline preview with modal expansion.
Use wider diagram layouts when useful.

mobile_rules: Place important actions inside reachable zones.
desktop_rules: Allow richer preview interactions only when useful.

mobile_rules: Sticky CTA active after hero scroll.
WhatsApp and phone actions remain easy to access.
Forms should reduce typing and use progressive steps.
desktop_rules: CTA should appear in hero, proof sections, case studies, and final conversion block.
Forms may show more fields but must remain short.

rules: Avoid heavy PDF embeds on mobile.
Delay high-resolution diagrams until user interaction.
Mirror layout direction for RTL languages.
Use logical spacing instead of hardcoded left/right values.
Preserve responsive hierarchy across all languages.
Allow translated text to expand without layout breakage.

failure_prevention: Do not use desktop grids on mobile.
Do not place CTA below first mobile scroll.
Do not show unreadable technical diagrams.
Do not use large uncompressed images.
Do not rely on hover interactions.
Do not stack too many technical elements in one viewport.
implementation_notes: Responsive behavior must be implemented mobile-first.
All components must be tested across mobile, tablet, desktop, and RTL layouts.
Technical readability and conversion access must not be sacrificed at smaller screen sizes.
Responsive rules should map directly to frontend breakpoints and design tokens.
